authoredNote: Source written first, expectation recorded from the post-fix analyzer run (script output quoted in the #855 report). The analyzer was NOT the broken layer, so this fixture is a REGRESSION pin rather than a red-to-green flip: it exists because the analyzer half must keep emitting the edge that the index layer now attributes.
rationale: M59 (#855): a call made from an anonymous-class member INITIALISER (a `val` inside `new Runnable { ... }`) must be emitted from the ANONYMOUS TYPE symbol, not from the enclosing method and not dropped. The sibling fixture scala/anonymous-body-scope pins a call made from a *def* inside an anonymous body, whose source is that def's own storeable symbol (`run`) — a shape that structurally cannot catch a lost attribution, which is why cats-effect TimeT.scala:148 could go silent with every gate green. Here the edge source is `anonymous_Runnable`, a name the store's artifact filter refuses to persist (src/ast/analysis-exclusions.ts `/^(anonymous|anon|unnamed)[_-]/i`), so the analyzer's emission and the index's attribution are two distinct contracts and this fixture pins the first. The `mirrored` def is the control: same call, same anonymous body, but a storeable source.

expectRelationships.comment: control: identical call from a storeable source in the same body

forbidRelationships.comment: the anonymous body's call must NOT be flattened onto the enclosing method by the ANALYZER (that flattening is the index layer's job, recorded in metadata.syntheticSource — never the emitter's)
the M37.21 #610 JD18 leak direction: members of an anonymous body attribute to the anonymous type
